newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-APEC nations seen using more gas, less oil.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-APEC nations seen using more gas, less oil.

text.p: Asia-Pacific countries are expected to use less oil and more gas in the future, an Indonesian energy official said on Monday.

"Currently, the region primarily utilises fossil energies, dominated by oil, coal and gas," Purnomo Yusgiantoro, adviser to Indonesia's minister of mines and energy, told a meeting of energy ministers and business executives from Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum nations.
"However, the composition of the energy mix in the future seems to shift away from oil use and more towards gas," Yusgiantoro said.
The reserves-to-production ratio of oil in the Asia-Pacific region is about 20 years, compared with around 60 years' worth of gas reserves, Yusgiantoro said.
"The deficit of oil in the region will most likely be supplied from external geographic areas and most probably this will increase our oil dependency on the Middle Eastern countries," he said.
The greater potential for gas means gas will be substituted for oil whenever possible, he said.
Meanwhile, future oil and gas development, including exploration and enhanced oil recovery, will require a greater capital investment and higher commitment of technology, Yusgiantoro said.
"Therefore, it is sensible to expect that the terms and conditions of the production-sharing contracts must be made more attractive to foreign direct investments or foreign oil companies," he said.

The situation is heightened by current high international oil prices, which will probably encourage host governments in the region to introduce more flexible fiscal policies to encourage exploration, he said.
In the case of Indonesia, there are still some 40 hydrocarbon basins that have potential for development, Yusgiantoro said.
The basins are located in eastern Indonesia and in the frontier zones, and have been earmarked through incentives for further exploration, he said.
